headline: Mistakes to Avoid When Changing Your Interior Floor Plan
articleBody:
Altering interior walls involves much more than drywall removal. Avoiding these common missteps keeps your project on schedule and protects your home's structural integrity.

Common Mistakes to Avoid:
- Assuming a wall is non-bearing: Never judge a wall solely by its sheetrock. Look in the attic or crawlspace to see how joists rest on top plates, or have a licensed professional confirm it.
- Overlooking hidden utilities: Wall cavities frequently hide plumbing stacks, electrical home runs, or central HVAC returns. Plan for relocation costs and chase routes ahead of time.
- Starting demolition before permits: Municipalities require scaled before-and-after floor plans showing room dimensions and uses. Demolishing early can trigger stop-work orders and fines.
- Compromising minimum passage widths: Removing a wall only to push traffic into an undersized walkway violates residential building standards. Keep hallways and entries comfortable and compliant.
- Neglecting flooring continuity: Taking out a wall leaves an exposed subfloor gap. Decide early whether you will weave in matching hardwood, add transitions, or replace flooring across the whole space.

What to Do Next
A successful reconfiguration relies on thoughtful drafting, proper engineering allowances, and coordinated trade work.
